description: Fresh-eyes review of the complete PKIX workspace. No git history anchor — code read on its own terms. Scope: all production source files in pkix-path, pkix-revocation, pkix-chain, pkix-chain-simple, pkix-path-builder, pkix-profiles.
notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — two real issues found: verify_simple max_path_len inconsistency (defense-in-depth gap, shape check masks it today) and pkix-profiles stubs returning wrong policy silently. No P0 correctness bugs found in the path validation or name matching logic. NormalizedIter is correct for v0.1 ASCII scope. PKITS §4.3 tests confirm the name normalization works.
Confidence: 10% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: (1) OCSP producedAt/thisUpdate interaction — I traced the logic but complex time edge cases could be wrong; (2) pathLenConstraint off-by-one for self-issued certs (PKITS 4.6.15-17 are ignored). Uncertainty driven by: not executing the OCSP validity-window edge cases against a live responder; not testing the self-issued-cert pathLen exemption path. Would raise confidence if: the ignored PKITS tests were implemented and passing.
Idiom rating: CLEAN — no unsafe, all pub error enums #[non_exhaustive], ? operator used throughout, no unwrap() in production code, iterator combinators used idiomatically. Only gap is missing Clone/Debug derives on CrlChecker/OcspChecker (PKIX-yo2.4) and the argument-order inconsistency in names_match (PKIX-yo2.5, opinion).
Rust idiom confidence: 5% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: none — clippy passes clean and I could not find any pattern that would make a serious Rust practitioner wince. Uncertainty driven by: not running cargo expand to inspect macro-generated code (none present here).
title: Review: entire PKIX codebase (fresh-eyes)
